_comment: Synthetic example - a health insurer's GenAI customer-service assistant on a hosted foundation model (deployer), RAG over policy conditions, with tools that look up the caller's own claim status. Limited risk (Art. 50 disclosure) — but health data in prompts, an external model provider (DORA), agentic tool calls and a 'not yet approved' governance status make it the case that looks easy and is not.
sys_owner: Example Health Insurer N.V. — Customer Contact
sys_description: A chat assistant on a hosted large language model that answers insured persons' questions about coverage and claims, retrieves the policy conditions and, after login, looks up the caller's own claim status through an internal API.
intended_purpose: First-line answers to coverage and claim-status questions; hand-off to a human agent for anything else. No decisions on coverage or payment.
data_sources: Policy conditions (public), help-centre articles, claim-status API (per caller), chat transcripts.
human_oversight: Agents monitor a live queue and can take over any conversation; a weekly sample of transcripts is scored for correctness; a wrong-answer report button is shown under every reply.
dg_data_owner: Head of Customer Contact (data domain: customer interaction)
dg_lineage: Policy conditions + help-centre CMS -> chunk + embed (nightly) -> vector store -> ZorgChat (hosted model, EU region) -> answer -> chat widget; claim-status tool: caller identity -> claims API (read-only) -> answer
dg_q_evidence: Knowledge-base freshness: nightly sync, max age 24 h (measured). Answer correctness sample: 94% (weekly review, 2026-08).

gov_exceptions.exception: Pilot with 5% of web-chat traffic before the approval decision
gov_exceptions.decision: Allowed with human take-over on every escalation and daily transcript review

gov_literacy.training: Working with ZorgChat: take-over, wrong-answer reporting, what the assistant may not answer
